working_title: Why your seat belt locks when you pull it fast

fact_sources.claim: Emergency locking retractors can respond to rapid webbing withdrawal or vehicle acceleration; designs differ by vehicle.
A rapid pull can make a web-sensing seat belt retractor lock until belt tension is released.

beats.visible_action: Person quickly pulls the belt and it stops short

beats.narration: A slow pull lets the strap unwind normally.
beats.visible_action: Same hand slowly pulls belt; inset spool rotates freely

beats.narration: A fast pull can trigger the emergency lock.
beats.visible_action: Hand pulls faster and the spool's locking state changes

beats.narration: The retractor stops more belt from feeding out.
beats.visible_action: Cutaway shows spool halted while belt becomes taut

beats.narration: Some retractors also respond to sudden vehicle movement.
beats.visible_action: Car decelerates; second trigger indicator changes state

beats.narration: But a gentle tug should still feel easy.
beats.visible_action: Side-by-side slow pull and fast pull compare their outcomes

beats.narration: Release the tension, then pull again slowly.
beats.visible_action: Person releases belt slightly; it retracts and then pulls normally

beats.narration: That sudden stop is a safety feature, not a jam.
beats.visible_action: Person buckles belt and camera returns to the original pull

loop_resolution: End on the same belt and hand as the opening, ready for the fast-pull cut. Internal latch geometry remains illustrative until checked against a specified retractor model.
